# Read a page with `web_fetch`

`web_fetch` gives an agent the content of a public webpage through the SerpApi Extract API.

## When to use it

Use it to read articles, documentation, and other pages the agent needs to summarize or cite. Pair it with [`web_search`](web_search.html) to find sources and then read the relevant pages.

Choose [`web_map`](web_map.html) to discover URLs within a website, or [`web_crawl`](web_crawl.html) to read several linked pages in one call.

## Quick example

```python
from serpapi_search_tools import web_fetch, web_search

agent_tools = [web_search(), web_fetch()]
```

With one supported SDK installed, these tools are native to that SDK. Add them to your agent's tool collection. See [Agent SDKs](frameworks.html) for setup and explicit provider selection when multiple SDKs are installed.

An agent can call `web_fetch` with a URL from its search results:

```json
{"url": "https://www.python.org/about/"}
```

## Inputs the agent can provide

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | yes | The absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL of the page to read |

The agent supplies only `url`. The tool fixes the Extract API operation to `scrape`; content filters and response settings stay in application code.

## Configure the tool

| Constructor option | Default | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | `"auto"` | Detect one installed SDK or select an SDK explicitly |
| `default_params` | `None` | Set content selectors and other Extract API settings |
| `mode` | `compact` | Select page Markdown for JSON output; use `"full"` to retain all JSON fields |
| `response_format` | `markdown` | Return the API's Markdown, or choose `"json"` for structured fields |
| `timeout` | `None` | Set the SDK request timeout in seconds |
| `name` | `"web_fetch"` | Give a configured page reader a distinct tool name |

The tool also accepts `api_key`, `client`, and `include_examples`. See [Common configuration](configuration.html) for authentication and shared options.

## Useful SerpApi parameters

Use CSS selectors to focus on the parts of a page the agent needs:

```python
from serpapi_search_tools import web_fetch

read_article = web_fetch(
    timeout=90,
    default_params={
        "include_tags": "main,article",
        "exclude_tags": "nav,footer,.ads",
        "timeout": 30000,
    },
    name="read_article",
)
agent_tools = [read_article]
```

`include_tags` keeps matching content; `exclude_tags` removes matching elements. Choose selectors that exist on the target pages. The constructor's `timeout` controls the SDK request in seconds, while `default_params["timeout"]` controls the API's page fetch in milliseconds. Other API settings include `device`, `prefetch_delay`, and `no_cache`.

## What comes back

Markdown output preserves the API response, including whitespace, headings, and links. For ordinary pages it contains the page content. If a Google or Bing search URL redirects to its dedicated engine, it can contain search results and metadata instead.

| Configuration | Returned value |
| --- | --- |
| Default, or any Markdown configuration | The API's Markdown unchanged |
| `response_format="json"` | A JSON string containing only `{"markdown":"..."}` |
| `mode="full", response_format="json"` | The complete JSON response |

Compact JSON raises `SerpApiSearchError` if `markdown` is missing or empty. Use full JSON to read metadata, structured page fields, or a redirected engine's response. Set `default_params={"include_markdown": False}` to omit Markdown from full JSON.

## Common mistakes

- Passing a search query or a relative path as `url`. Find a page with `web_search` first, then pass its full URL.
- Expecting JavaScript to run. The Extract API reads the fetched page without executing JavaScript.
- Using content selectors that match nothing on the page.
- Using the constructor's `mode` to change the API operation. Choose `web_map` or `web_crawl` for other operations; `mode` controls JSON response detail.
